Subject: SLO handshake: prompt pack, harness handoff, and reproducibility plan

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a performance qualification run:

1) Target SLOs you confirmed on the call
   - 95th p99 latency (token-generation) target: 350ms/prompt (p50 target 120ms)
   - Sustained throughput target: 300 reqs/min for the search/assistant route (avg payload ~420 tokens)
   - Concurrency target: baseline 8 concurrent streams, spike tolerance to 24 for 30s bursts
   - Streaming: chunk size ~64 tokens, client requires <150ms time-to-first-chunk

2) What we need from StrataHealth to run a meaningful harness
   - Seed prompt set (10-20 representative examples) + flag which prompts must be reproduced verbatim (PII redaction in place)
   - Representative payload sizes (min/median/max tokens for request and expected completion)
   - Clarify whether client-side pre/post-processing will happen synchronously (affects end-to-end latency)

3) What Redwood will deliver for the qualification run
   - A reproducible harness run (attached: redwood_harness_instructions_v1.yaml) with measurement definitions (attached: measurement-definitions.md)
   - Prompt pack ingestion template (attached: strata_prompt_seed_v1.csv) and a small script to canonicalize token accounting
   - Raw token-level timing and KV-cache hit/miss logs for reproducibility

4) Proposed timeline
   - Aisha sends prompt pack + sample payloads: by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-08)
   - Redwood runs baseline and posts initial run artifacts: +48 hours after receipt
   - Follow-up readout + action items: 2026-12-13 (15-minute sync)

Action for you: please confirm the streaming requirement around TTFChunk (is 150ms strict TTF or a best-effort) and upload the prompt pack to the Drive link below.

Drive link for uploads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_prompt-pack
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/78321

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben in for harness details once you confirm the pack.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: strata_prompt_seed_v1.csv (seed prompts), redwood_harness_instructions_v1.yaml (harness runbook), measurement-definitions.md (measurement glossary)

Mateo —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:

- 150ms is a soft target for time-to-first-chunk; our product team wants it to be as close to 150ms as possible for interactive sessions, but tolerances are +/-50ms for the proof-of-concept.
- We'll provide 15 seed prompts that cover search, clarification, and multi-turn assistant flows. Payload sizes: min 64 tokens, median 420 tokens, max 1,200 tokens (we will redact any PHI before upload).
- Pre/post-processing: we do synchronous post-processing for reranking steps which will be applied client-side after the completion stream. For streaming latency, please measure to the client-facing first-chunk event (inclusive of Redwood runtime, exclusive of client-side processing).

I uploaded an initial seed file to the Drive folder (strata_seed_sample_v1.csv) and cc'd our infra alias with the sample payload shapes. If you need a matched set of expected completions or automated evaluation labels, say the word and I can pull those from our offline test harness (may take 24–48 hours).

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Malik
Sr. Product Manager, Search | StrataHealth

Looping in engineering detail so we can pin measurement definitions. Key clarifications from our side:

- "Latency" definitions: we will report (a) server-side TTFChunk (time from request ingress to first token chunk emitted by runtime), (b) full-response generation time (server-side), and (c) end-to-end as measured by an optional synthetic client (includes network to the client VM). We will label each trace accordingly.
- Token accounting: we'll run the pack through our tokenizer and provide per-prompt input_token_count and output_token_count. That will let us normalize throughput across payload shapes.
- Concurrency/throughput plan for the run: baseline run will be 8 concurrent workers at a steady arrival rate of 5 reqs/sec (per-worker), sustained for 10 minutes; spike run will ramp to 24 concurrent workers for 60s bursts. We will repeat each scenario 3x for stability.
- Streaming measurement: we will emit per-chunk timestamps and chunk sizes. For the Strata metric you care about (TTFChunk <=150ms), Ben: we'll flag any TTFChunk >220ms as an incident for the run and compute percent above threshold.

I pushed the harness playbook and a sample YAML to the internal harness URL (internal link below). The attachments Mateo referenced are good starting points; I added a small script that canonicalizes the CSV into the run format.

Internal harness: https://internal.redwood.ai/harness/RW-HARN-58

If Strata can provide expected completions, we can also compute simple correctness metrics (BLEU, ROUGE-lite, and a small semantic-similarity checkpoint). Otherwise we'll focus strictly on performance reproducibility.

—Ben
